look_here_first: LOOK AT THE PAIRED GREEN BRACTS, NOT A RED LEAF SPOT. E. roemeriana is a small annual upright or basally reclining spurge (15–30 cm) with hairless, entire, obovate-to-oblanceolate leaves. Each flowering branch repeatedly forks; in the center find a tiny cyathium framed by TWO rounded green dichasial bracts that are JOINED for about HALF their length, creating a shallow cup. Tiny bright yellow gland structures have SHORT somewhat convergent horns; a smooth, roundish 3-lobed capsule develops nearby. Against E. commutata, the key is CONSISTENT substantial bract fusion rather than distinct or only barely joined pairs. E. longicruris instead has numerous tightly OVERLAPPING cup/leaf-like terminal bracts; E. austrotexana has far narrower leaves and distinct non-overlapping bracts. Mature E. roemeriana seeds have randomly scattered DEEP BROAD PITS and a prominent caruncle; two photographed mature seeds now show pits and caruncles; their absolute size is not photo-calibrated. This taxon has published HAYS COUNTY records in spring-fed Edwards Plateau limestone stream valleys, but the project's formal native-by-county certification remains on hold.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbiaceae, Euphorbia subg. Esula sect. Tithymalus. The yellow structures are tiny cyathia (specialized pseudanthia), not ordinary petals, and nearby smooth 3-lobed structures are developing fruits.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Annual taprooted small spring herb, erect or sometimes reclining near base, 15–30 cm, glabrous; limestone stream valleys, rich calcareous soils, spring-fed creek canyons and floodplain terraces of the eastern Edwards Plateau.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Main leafy stem: alternate leaves, blade oblanceolate to obovate about 5–20 × 5–10 mm, entire margins, cuneate/attenuate base, rounded tip, hairless faces, pinnate veins; petioles 2–5 mm.

key_traits.label: Branching
key_traits.text: Terminal pleiochasium normally forks into 3 branches, repeatedly subdividing 1–4 times into 2-part branches; larger upper bracts similar in shape to obovate main leaves.

key_traits.label: Dichasial bracts
key_traits.text: Key: each CYATHIUM sits between paired broad green reniform-to-semicircular bracts, FUSED to about 1/2 their length; no teeth, rounded or obtuse tips. Existing single closeup shows a cup-like pair but exact fusion percentage remains noncalibrated and partly overlapped.

key_traits.label: Cyathia
key_traits.text: Tiny terminal cup/involucre 1.5–2 × 1–1.6 mm, glabrous, with FOUR elliptic-to-trapezoid nectar glands 0.4–0.6 × 0.7–1.2 mm and short 0.1–0.3 mm slightly convergent horns. The prominent yellow parts are gland structures, not conventional flower petals.

key_traits.label: Capsules
key_traits.text: Smooth, glabrous, subglobose slightly 3-lobed capsule about 2–2.5 × 2.4–3 mm. The image has developing green fruit, but cannot establish the measured diameter.

key_traits.label: Seeds
key_traits.text: Brown oblong-ovoid seeds 1.6–1.8 × 1.4–1.5 mm, with widely scattered deep and broad pits rather than regular ridges. A conic- or kidney-shaped caruncle approximately 0.3–0.4 × 0.4–0.6 mm. Need confirmed ripe loose seed photograph with millimeter scale.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: TWO green round/reniform dichasial bracts FUSED roughly HALF their length, forming cup below cyathium

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Yellow horned gland structures at tiny cyathium (not true petals)

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Glabrous obovate/oblanceolate small leaves with entire margins

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Spring-flowering small 15–30cm annual of calcareous creekside habitat

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Smooth 3-lobed capsule and brown mature seeds with DEEP SCATTERED PITS plus caruncle

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Differentiate from E. commutata (separate or basally barely joined bracts) and E. longicruris (strongly overlapping terminal bracts)
